knackRulesIntro: Schwimmen uses a 32-card deck from seven through ace and is played by two to six people. This implementation uses the common layout with three face-up center cards.
knackRulesGoalBody: Make the highest possible value with your three cards. Only the best total in one suit counts. The lowest value at the end of a round loses a life.
knackRules_setupBody: Everyone receives three private cards. Three more cards lie face up in the center, and the remaining stock stays face down.
knackRules_scoreBody: An ace is eleven; kings, queens, jacks, and tens are ten; number cards use their face value. Only cards of one suit are added. Three equal ranks score 30.5. Three aces are Fire, the top combination; an ace plus two ten-value cards of one suit makes 31.
knackRules_turnBody: On your turn, exchange exactly one hand card for exactly one center card, or exchange all three hand cards for all three center cards. You may never exchange exactly two cards.
knackRules_passBody: You may pass instead of exchanging. If every active player passes consecutively, the three center cards are discarded and replaced from the stock. If fewer than three remain, the round is scored.
knackRules_knockBody: You may knock instead of exchanging. Every other active player then receives exactly one final turn before scoring; the player who knocked does not play again.
knackRules_roundBody: A 31 or Fire ends the round immediately. Fire makes every other active player lose one life. Otherwise, everyone tied for the lowest score loses a life.
knackRules_livesBody: Everyone begins with three lives. After losing the last life, a player is swimming and remains in the game. Their next loss eliminates them.
knackRulesEndBody: The last player who has not been eliminated wins.

mauMauRulesIntro: Mau-Mau uses a 32-card deck from seven through ace and is played by two to six people.
mauMauRulesGoalBody: Be the first to discard all five cards in your hand. The suit and rank of the top discard determine which card can follow.
mauMauRules_setupBody: Everyone receives five cards. A normal card without a special effect starts the face-up discard pile, and the remaining cards form the face-down stock.
mauMauRules_playBody: Play exactly one card whose suit or rank matches the top discard. A jack is the exception and always fits. Play then normally passes clockwise.
mauMauRules_drawBody: If no card in your hand fits, draw exactly one. If it fits, you may play it immediately or keep it. If it does not fit, your turn ends automatically.
mauMauRules_sevenBody: After a seven, the next player draws two cards and is skipped.
mauMauRules_eightBody: After an eight, the next player is skipped. In a two-player game, this gives the same player another turn.
mauMauRules_jackBody: A jack can be played on any card. When playing it, choose clubs, diamonds, hearts, or spades; the next play must match that suit.
mauMauRules_stockBody: When the stock is empty, the top discard remains in place. All older discards are shuffled to form a new stock.
mauMauRulesEndBody: The first player to play their final card legally wins immediately.
rulesIntro: Podkidnoy Durak is played by two to six people. There are no teams: everyone tries to get rid of their own cards before the others.
rulesGoalBody: Once the draw pile is empty, players who have no cards left finish successfully. The only person still holding cards at the end is the Durak and loses.
rules_setupBody: Each player receives six cards. A card at the draw pile determines the trump suit. The player holding the lowest trump makes the first attack.
rules_attackBody: The attacker places any card or several cards of the same rank from their hand face up on the table. The next active player in seating order is the defender.
rules_defenseBody: The defender must beat every attack separately, either with a higher card of the same suit or with a trump. A trump can only be beaten by a higher trump.
rules_throwInBody: After all open attacks have been covered, the attackers may throw in cards in turn. Every new card's rank must already appear on the table. A round allows no more than six attack cards and never more than the defender held at its start.
rules_takeBody: If the defender cannot or does not want to cover everything, they choose “Pick up cards”. The round ends immediately and the defender takes every attack and defense card into their hand; no more cards may be thrown in.
rules_roundEndBody: If every card was covered and all attackers pass, the table cards leave the game and the previous defender attacks next. After a pickup, the defender is skipped. Starting with the original attacker, players draw back up to six cards; the defender draws last.
rulesGameEndBody: Once the pile is exhausted, no more cards are drawn. A player with no cards is finished. The last person holding cards loses as the Durak. If all remaining players discard their final cards together, the game ends in a draw.

rommeRulesIntro: This is the German melding form of Rummy, played with two full decks and six jokers.
rommeRulesGoalBody: Make valid sets and runs, lay cards off on table melds, and be the first player to empty your hand.
rommeRules_setupBody: Each player receives 13 cards. One card starts the face-up discard pile and the rest form the face-down stock.
rommeRules_drawBody: At the start of every turn, take either the top card of the stock or the top face-up discard.
rommeRules_meldsBody: A set is three or four equal ranks in different suits. A run is at least three consecutive cards of one suit. An ace may be low before two or high after king, but cannot wrap around. Jokers replace missing cards.
rommeRules_openingBody: Your first melds must jointly reach the minimum selected in the lobby, normally 40 points. Face cards count 10, aces 11, and number cards their face value.
rommeRules_layoffBody: After completing your initial meld, you may add fitting hand cards to any meld already on the table.
rommeRules_jokerBody: After your initial meld, you may replace a joker with the natural card it represents. In a set, this must complete all four suits. The recovered joker must immediately be used with selected hand cards in a new valid meld.
rommeRules_discardBody: Discard exactly one hand card face up. Play then passes clockwise.
rommeRules_stockBody: When the stock runs out, all but the top discard are shuffled to make a new stock.
rommeRulesEndBody: The first player with no cards after discarding wins. Remaining hand cards count as penalty points; a joker is worth 20.
ginRulesIntro: Gin Rummy is the quick two-player Rummy variant played with one deck and no jokers. Melds remain concealed in your hand during play.
canastaRulesIntro: Classic Canasta is played by four people in two fixed partnerships with 108 cards.
canastaRulesGoalBody: Your team builds same-rank melds, completes canastas of at least seven cards, and is first to reach the selected target score.
canastaRules_teamsBody: Seating order creates two teams: the first and third players partner, as do the second and fourth. Melds and scores belong to the whole team.
canastaRules_setupBody: Each player receives eleven cards. The rest form the stock and one face-up card starts the discard pile. A starting wild card or red three freezes the pile.
canastaRules_threesBody: Red threes are exposed immediately and replaced when drawn from the stock. A black three on top prevents the next player from taking the discard pile.
canastaRules_drawBody: Start each turn by drawing one stock card or, when eligible, taking the entire discard pile. You may then meld and finish by discarding one card.
canastaRules_meldsBody: A meld contains at least three cards of one rank and at least two natural cards. Twos and jokers are wild, with no more than three wild cards per meld. Seven or more cards make a canasta.
canastaRules_openingBody: A team's first meld must total at least 15, 50, 90, or 120 card points depending on its current score. Multiple melds may combine to meet the requirement.
canastaRules_discardPileBody: The top discard must be melded immediately. If the pile is frozen or your team has not opened, you need two matching natural cards in hand; otherwise an existing team meld may also make the pile available.
canastaRules_goingOutBody: End the round by melding every card or discarding your final card. When the option is enabled, your team must first complete at least one canasta.
canastaRules_scoringBody: Melded cards score positively and hand cards negatively. Natural canastas score 500, mixed canastas 300, and going out 100 bonus points. Red threes score 100 each or 800 for all four; without a meld they are penalties.
canastaRulesEndBody: When a team reaches the selected target after a round, the partnership with the higher total wins.
ginRulesGoalBody: Arrange as many cards as possible into sets and runs while keeping the value of unmatched cards, called deadwood, low. Be first to reach the target score selected in the lobby.
ginRules_setupBody: Exactly two players use a 52-card deck without jokers. Each receives 10 cards and one card starts the face-up discard. An ace is worth 1 and may only precede a two.
ginRules_meldsBody: A set contains three or four cards of one rank. A run contains at least three consecutive cards of one suit. Melds are detected automatically and stay in hand until the round ends.
ginRules_openingBody: The non-dealer may first take the upcard or pass, followed by the dealer. If both pass, the non-dealer draws from the stock.
ginRules_turnBody: Draw the face-up card or a card from the stock, then discard exactly one card. Play passes to the other player.
ginRules_knockBody: After drawing, you may knock with your discard if your remaining deadwood is worth no more than 10 points. With zero deadwood, you declare Gin.
ginRules_layoffBody: After a normal knock, the opponent may add fitting deadwood cards to the knocker's melds. Laying off is not allowed against Gin.
ginRules_stockBody: If the third-last stock card is drawn and nobody knocks, the round ends without scoring. The same player deals the next round.
ginRules_scoringBody: The winner scores the deadwood difference plus a 10-point box bonus. Gin adds 25 points. If the opponent is tied or lower after laying off, they undercut and receive an additional 20 points.
ginRulesEndBody: The dealer alternates after each scored round. The first player to reach or exceed the selected target score wins the game.
spadesRulesIntro: Spades uses a 52-card deck and is played by four players in two fixed partnerships. Opposite players are partners and spades are always trump.
spadesRulesGoalBody: Together, predict as accurately as possible how many tricks your team will win and be the first team to reach the target score.
spadesRules_setupBody: All 52 cards are dealt, giving each player 13 cards. Partners alternate in the play order.
spadesRules_biddingBody: Starting left of the dealer, every player makes one bid from 0 to 13. The partners' bids form the team contract.
spadesRules_nilBody: A bid of zero is Nil. Winning no tricks earns the configured bonus; taking even one trick incurs the same penalty. The partner's team contract still applies.
spadesRules_playBody: Players must follow the led suit when possible. Otherwise any card may be played, including a spade. Spades cannot be led until broken unless the hand contains only spades.
spadesRules_scoringBody: A made team contract scores ten points per bid trick plus one point per overtrick. A failed contract loses ten points per bid trick.
spadesRules_bagsBody: Overtricks accumulate as bags. When the sandbag rule is enabled, every ten bags deduct 100 points and are then removed.
spadesRulesEndBody: Once at least one team reaches the target and the scores are not tied, the higher-scoring team wins. A tie causes another round.
ohHellRulesIntro: Oh Hell! is a 52-card trick-taking game for three to seven players. Each player tries to make their bid exactly in every round.
ohHellRulesGoalBody: Score the most points over all rounds by winning exactly as many tricks as you bid.
ohHellRules_setupBody: The player left of the dealer bids first and leads the first trick. After the deal, the next face-up card determines trump.
ohHellRules_scheduleBody: Depending on player count, hands begin with at most ten cards. Hand size falls to one card and then rises to the starting size again.
ohHellRules_biddingBody: Each player bids from zero up to the current hand size. Passing is not allowed.
ohHellRules_dealerBody: When enabled, the dealer bidding last may not make the sum of all bids equal the number of available tricks.
ohHellRules_playBody: Players must follow the led suit when possible. Otherwise any card may be played. The highest trump wins, or the highest card of the led suit if no trump was played.
ohHellRules_scoringBody: An exact bid scores the configured bonus plus one point per trick. A missed bid scores its tricks only when that lobby option is enabled.
ohHellRulesEndBody: After the final ascending round, the highest score wins. Players tied for the highest score share the win.
cheatRulesIntro: Cheat is a bluffing shedding game. Cards are played face down and their claimed rank is announced; the claim may be a lie.
cheatRulesGoalBody: Be first to empty your hand and survive the possible challenge to your final claim.
cheatRules_setupBody: One or two complete 52-card decks are dealt as evenly as possible. Small differences in hand size are allowed.
cheatRules_sequenceBody: The required claim follows the selected sequence: ace, two through king, or downward from ace through king to two, then starts again.
cheatRules_playBody: On your turn, play at least one card face down and claim that every card has the required rank. The actual cards may be anything.
cheatRules_challengeBody: Until the next play, any other player may challenge the most recent claim. Only the cards from that play are revealed for verification.
cheatRules_pickupBody: If at least one card was wrong, the bluffing player takes the whole pile. If all were correct, the challenger takes it.
cheatRules_finalPlayBody: A player who plays their final cards wins only after the claim is accepted or unsuccessfully challenged. An exposed bluff continues the game.
cheatRulesEndBody: The first player with no cards whose final claim stands wins.
skatRulesIntro: Skat uses 32 cards. Exactly three players take part in each deal; at a four-player table the dealer sits out. Under the International Skat Order, the winner of the bidding plays alone against the other two.
skatRulesGoalBody: The declarer must fulfill the chosen contract. A suit or Grand game requires at least 61 of the 120 card points; in a Null game the declarer must avoid every trick.
skatRules_setupBody: Clockwise, forehand, middlehand, and rearhand each receive ten cards in packets of 3–4–3. Two cards form the face-down skat. With four players, the dealer sits out that deal.
skatRules_biddingBody: Middlehand first bids against forehand, then rearhand bids against that contest's winner. Only valid, increasing game values may be called. The highest bidder or holder becomes declarer. If everyone passes, the deal is recorded without a score and the next dealer deals.
skatRules_skatTitle: Taking the skat or playing hand
skatRules_skatBody: The declarer either picks up the skat and discards exactly two cards face down, or leaves it untouched and plays a hand game. The skat cards always count as part of the declarer's holding and card points when scoring.
skatRules_contractsBody: In a suit game all four jacks and the named suit are trumps. In Grand only the jacks are trumps. Null has no trumps and ranks cards ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven.
skatRules_announcementsBody: Schneider and Schwarz may only be announced in a hand game. Schneider requires at least 90 card points and Schwarz all ten tricks. Ouvert exposes the declarer's cards; in suit and Grand the declarer must also win every trick. Null Ouvert is possible with or without picking up the skat.
skatRules_playBody: Forehand leads the first trick; each later trick is led by the previous winner. Players must follow the led suit or trump category when able. Otherwise any card may be played. In suit and Grand the plain-suit order is ace, ten, king, queen, nine, eight, seven; the jacks are the highest trumps in clubs, spades, hearts, diamonds order.
skatRules_scoringBody: Suit and Grand values derive from their base value, matadors, and game levels; Null contracts have fixed values of 23, 35, 46, or 59. A won game scores its value, while a lost game loses twice its value. If the final game value is below the bid, the contract is lost regardless of the tricks won.
skatRules_seriesBody: The dealer rotates after every deal. The selected number of dealing rounds ensures everyone deals equally often. With tournament scoring enabled, a win receives 50 extra points; a loss costs another 50, and the other players receive the official opponent points.
skatRulesEndBody: After the configured number of deals, the highest total score wins. Players tied for the highest score share the win.
